output.brief: The FCR drop is most likely caused by the 14 April Finance change, not by the new starters. FC-0417 cut the in-call credit limit from £100 to £25 and automatically refers larger billing adjustments to the Billing Resolution team. Billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% in the same week FCR fell. Referred calls resolve first time only about 34% of the time, against 82% for non-referred calls. The referral rate is about the same for the April intake (56%) and for tenured agents (53–54%). Tenured agents' FCR fell by the same amount as the new starters' (about 8 points), so inexperience does not explain it. The tariff-driven mix shift is small: tariff enquiries still resolve at 85%. I did not test the IVR redesign or workload explanations, so I can't rule them out as smaller contributors. I'm fairly confident in the main finding. Next step: do not put the April intake on performance plans. Agree a revised credit limit with Finance, backed by post-call sampling, and trial it on two teams for six weeks. The limit is a configuration setting that can be changed in one working day. Track FCR and the unsupported-credit rate during the trial. Finance has said it would consider a higher limit on exactly those terms.
